text:
maria: Quick east-west quicktake — I ran a focused microbench for embeddings + small-chat across our 3 GPU types (L4, T4, A10G). Goal: capture p50/p95, tokens/sec, and crude $/1M tokens for capacity sizing and kernel lane choices. Posting highlights so we can decide canary targets.

devin: TL;DR before we dive: A10G wins raw throughput, L4 has the best cost-performance for single-instance chat latency in many configs, T4 still cheapest per-hour but needs more replicas to hit p95 targets. Spreadsheet: https://go/bench/tri-gpu-2123 (internal).

benchbot: automated run summary (region: us-west / eu-west). run id: tri-2123. configs: {model: small-chat-v1, embed-model: embed-lite-v1, seq: 256/64, q: q4f16/q8f32, kernels: fused-attn-v2, generic}.

benchbot: EMBEDDINGS (batch=64, 512-d vectors) — tokens not applicable, requests/sec shown:
- A10G: 420 req/s median (us-west) — p95 510
- L4: 360 req/s median — p95 430
- T4: 210 req/s median — p95 290
Approx $/1M req (GPU-only amortized): A10G ~$9.1, L4 ~$6.8, T4 ~$3.9

benchbot: SMALL-CHAT (seq=256 prompt + gen=64, continuous batching enabled) — gen tokens/sec and latency (median / p95):
- A10G: 55 tok/s, p50 ~220ms, p95 ~560ms, cost/1M gen-toks ~$8.8
- L4: 48 tok/s, p50 ~190ms, p95 ~420ms, cost/1M gen-toks ~$6.3
- T4: 32 tok/s, p50 ~320ms, p95 ~980ms, cost/1M gen-toks ~$3.2

ravi: Noticed kernel differences matter a lot for L4 on chat — fused-attn-v2 + optimized KV-cache cut p95 by ~120ms relative to the generic kernel. On A10G, kernel delta was smaller (~20-30ms).

sara: Quant notes: q4f16 stable for embeddings across all GPUs. For small-chat: q4 shows occasional token-stall on T4 with fused-attn-v2 (small but measurable regressions on some prompts). L4+q4 was OK but verify on the eval suite.

devin: Region delta: us-west vs eu-west — A10G us-west had ~8% higher throughput than eu-west (kernel availability + driver). L4 differences <4%. For capacity sizing, prefer L4 in eu region for chat-heavy workloads if price band matters.

jules: Can we share a compact recommendation matrix? My first pass:
- embeddings (high QPS): pick A10G if you need peak throughput and can pay, L4 if you want balance, T4 if cost-first (expect more nodes).
- small-chat (low-latency p95 focus): L4 recommended for canary; A10G for scale; T4 only for very cheap, non-p95-sensitive workloads.

maria: Agree. Also: for rollout, suggest canary lane = L4 + fused-attn-v2 + q4f16 for chat, and A10G + q8 for embeddings. Keep T4 in fallback pool for bulk offline or cheap embedding backfills.

devin: A few concrete numbers for canary SLOs: target p95 < 500ms for small-chat with 95% of traffic routed to canary under normal load. L4 config above meets that in us-west and eu-west in our microbench. T4 does not without >1.5x replicas.

benchbot: example bench command we used:
```
./run_microbench --model small-chat-v1 --gpu L4 --seq 256 --quant q4f16 --kernel fused-attn-v2 --batch 16 --duration 300
```

ravi: Follow-ups:
- run the sweep on apac (ap-southeast) to surface driver/kernel differences there.
- run the eval suite (1000 prompts) on q4f16 L4 to catch regressions before canary.
- build cost simulator (per-route) with these numbers to recommend autoscale limits.

sara: I'll queue the eval suite run and post results. Also will add a small prompt-level diff log for any generation regressions (BLEU/ROUGE-ish + human spot checks).

maria: Action items: (1) ravi -> apac sweep (ETA 48h), (2) sara -> eval suite q4-l4 (ETA 24h), (3) devin -> update canary config in the console + add fallback policy to route to T4 if p95 > threshold (ETA 72h). I'll update the model map after results.

devin: noop — noted. tagging @sre for capacity planning once apac numbers land. :thumbsup:

jules: thanks all — this quicktake helps a lot. we should surface a short summary slide for the next infra sync.

maria: +1 — I'll draft a 1-slide summary after we get apac numbers.
